source.citation: Unidentified correspondent, letter on opium and morphine habits, Medical Record 31–32 (1887): 595. Author to confirm from the page image.

inferred: reported.age (described only as a young lady)

complaints: seven years of eating morphine, ten to twenty grains a day
every specific cure her family bought has failed
presentation.course: Given morphine powders, to be taken as needed, during several months of pleurisy on the right side. The habit grew and has lasted seven years.
presentation.priorTreatment: Many advertised "specifics" for the opium habit, paid for by her family, without effect.

periodDiagnosis: opium or morphine habit begun under medical prescription

treatments.treatment: gained her confidence; good hygiene, useful occupation, iron tonics and a full diet; phosphorus, nux vomica, cannabis, digitalis; bromides for sleep
morphine given daily without her knowing the dose, reduced by a quarter to half a grain every other day; she was never allowed to refill her own bottles
treatments.response: cured in six months; no morphine and no craving six months later

outcome: Free of morphine at least six months after a six-month taper.
quotes: Morphine powders were pre- scribed by her physicians, to be used pro re nata.
in six months my little patient was cured

modernReading.text: Opioid dependence that began with a prescription for pleuritic pain. A slow taper with the patient's cooperation is still a reasonable approach; the concealed dosing would now be thought unethical.

fixed: habit began with a doctor's morphine prescription for a painful illness
years of daily use at a high dose

constrained.rule: comfortable or better; the family can pay for cures and a doctor
the family may raise the habit before the patient does

notes: The same letter describes opium smoking and morphine injection among Chinese and white smokers in a "Chinatown"; the city is not named in the excerpt.
